messages:
sara: alert from SIEM — unusual spike in high-cardinality SELECTs from service account `data-sync-sa` between 03:12-03:18 UTC. Saw simultaneous reads across users.*, events.* and billing.* tables. :eyes:
kevin: can you paste the alert details / query patterns?
sara: log excerpt:
```
2026-02-12T03:14:07Z QUERY user1234 data-sync-sa SELECT user_id, email, config FROM users WHERE updated_at > '2025-01-01' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10000
2026-02-12T03:14:08Z QUERY user1234 data-sync-sa SELECT * FROM events WHERE created_at > '2025-01-01' LIMIT 50000
2026-02-12T03:15:02Z QUERY user1234 data-sync-sa SELECT invoice_id, amount, payer FROM billing.payments WHERE status != 'refunded' LIMIT 20000
```
sara: also note: the access pattern starts ~10m after an RBAC role update pushed yesterday to give data-sync-sa "read_all" at org level. we rolled that change 02/11 22:50 UTC.
maria: :lock: ok first actions — rotate the SA token and remove the org-level read grant. can infra revoke immediately?
dylan: rotating now. running `authctl revoke-service-token data-sync-sa`
infra-bot: revoke request accepted, token revoked for data-sync-sa at 03:16:22Z. New token issuance blocked until review.
sara: thanks. can someone confirm audit logs show no data egress to an external host? SIEM says all queries returned, but no large outbound transfers detected.
kevin: checking firewall/proxy logs and object store egress. preliminary: no big s3 PUTs or external IP connections from DB host during window. only internal app responses.
maria: good. next: KMS check — did data-sync-sa have access to any customer-specific KMS keys?
dylan: looked at KMS policies — data-sync-sa had decrypt on two service keys used by internal batch jobs, not customer keys. those keys' usage shows no decrypt activity during spike window.
sara: so containment = revoked token, RBAC rollback, block new tokens, rotate creds, and check KMS usage. any additional comms?
maria: internal incident ticket and paging to product security + customer success for any flagged accounts touched. I'll raise a P0 ticket and notify Legal.
kevin: on mitigation: add rate limit rule on DB proxy for service accounts to cap rows returned per minute, and add anomaly rule for cross-schema multi-table selects.
dylan: putting a temporary query-rate-limit of 10k rows/min for service accounts now. will push permanent rule after postmortem.
incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0212-01 — Data access anomaly (service account high-volume reads). Triage owner: maria.
sara: next steps for post-incident: 1) confirm no customer data left the VPC 2) add automated alert for role-change followed by high-volume reads within 30m 3) require MFAs for RBAC changes to org-level grants 4) document runbook update.
maria: agree. I'll assign owners in the ticket. Also recommend we add audit logs retention to 90 days for quick historical checks.
kevin: will add a query fingerprinting snapshot around suspicious sessions so we can diff later. e.g., store top-n query hashes per session.
sara: any evidence this was malicious vs a bug in the sync job after role expand?
dylan: early suspicion: a bug in a cron batch that didn't paginate properly when it got higher permissions. stack traces show the job attempted to fetch next pages but misinterpreted header, so it used `LIMIT 50000` instead of using cursor flow.
maria: action: dev team must push a fix that switches to cursor-based pagination and add unit-tests that simulate permission changes. verify in staging.
kevin: I'll follow up with telemetry to add a correlation alert: if a role-grant event for a service account occurs, create a 30m elevated watch for large selects.
sara: thanks all. I'll keep channel updated. tagging @customer-success for possible outreach if we find customer-rows accessed.
maria: closing loop: rotate the two service keys used by data-sync-sa and schedule a quick postmortem doc within 48h. :white_check_mark:
